overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by not promptly admitting a member of the public from a Zoom waiting room and by failing to announce remote members (de minimis); recording allegation declined.

allegations.summary: A member of the public was denied access to a remote Zoom meeting; he waited in the waiting room from 7:16 p.m. and was never admitted.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to promptly admit Mr. Wood from the waiting room into the meeting, or indeed at all, the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The chair did not announce at the start of the all-remote meeting the names of members participating remotely, as 940 CMR 29.10(7)(b) requires.
The meeting was convened before Georgetown Community Television began recording it, which the complainant said was improper.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission's immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
